The Pitot Tube As mentioned previously, the tube measuring the total pressure in Figure 1.10 is called the Pitot tube, which, along with static pressure, is used for measuring the airspeed of an airplane. Several Pitot tubes can be seen on the front of the large jets at the airport. A single Pitot tube can be seen protruding (or hanging) from the wing of small airplanes. The hole that measures the static pressure of the air is the static port. This port is usu- ally on the side of the airplane fuselage near the front, though it is also occasionally placed on the side of the Pitot tube itself.
